title: The roadmap with four dates
scenario:
You are the COO of an HR services company with 1,200 staff. Your AI lead drew the first AI roadmap for the board. It has four items and four dates. The company uses Anthropic's API.

The board chair asks you: "Can I trust these dates?" The exhibit shows the draft and one vendor fact.
exhibit:
AI roadmap: DRAFT (use cases and owners are made-up; model facts from Anthropic's deprecations page, checked 2026-10-06)

#  Use                              Tier    Start    Owner   Needs first
A  Meeting summaries for all staff  low     Q4 2026  Ops     nothing
B  Claims helper that pays claims   high    Q4 2026  (none)  approval step: not planned
   up to EUR 300                                             audit logs: off
C  Customer chat assistant          medium  Q1 2027  Web     built on claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929
D  Underwriting agent team          high    Q1 2027  Risk    clean policy data: not planned

Vendor facts
  claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929: Deprecated 30 Sept 2026.
  Retirement 30 Nov 2026. Recommended replacement: claude-sonnet-5-5.

Notes from the AI lead
  - 6 API keys exist. Nobody knows which teams call that model.

questions.prompt: Item C starts in Q1 2027 on claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929. What should the roadmap say?

options.text: Launch on the old model in January, and move to a new one after the launch.
options.explanation: The page says requests to a retired model fail. The model retires on 30 Nov 2026, before the planned start.

options.text: Keep the plan, because the vendor will extend the retirement date for customers.
options.explanation: The page gives no such promise. It says to move to the replacement before the retirement date.

options.text: Delay item C until the vendor lists a replacement, and then restart the design.
options.explanation: The page already lists a replacement. Waiting adds delay without new information.

options.text: Plan item C on the recommended replacement, and add a test of it before the launch.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's page advises testing newer models well before retirement. A model-change row keeps this on the roadmap.

questions.prompt: Item B is a high-tier item in Q4 2026 with no owner, no approval step and audit logs off. What is the best change?

options.text: Keep B in Q4 2026, and only add an owner, since the tier is already marked.
options.explanation: An owner helps, but a high-tier action with no approval step or logs is still unsafe to start.

options.text: Move B to Next, and add lines for the approval step and logs, each with an owner.
options.explanation: Right. The lesson says prerequisites get their own lines, and a high-tier item starts only when its controls exist.

options.text: Delete B, because no AI use that pays claims can ever be approved.
options.explanation: The lesson does not forbid high-tier uses. It asks for the right controls first.

options.text: Move B to Later with no owner, so nobody needs to plan anything for it yet.
options.explanation: A good idea can wait in Later, but the missing controls still need owners when B comes forward.

questions.prompt: Item D is an agent team that needs clean policy data, which has no line on the roadmap. What is the best fix?

options.text: Add a data-cleanup line with an owner first, and start D as one simple workflow.
options.explanation: Right. Dependencies get their own lines. Anthropic's post says to find the simplest solution and add complexity only when needed.

options.text: Keep D as it is, and let the Risk team find out about the data problem later.
options.explanation: The missing prerequisite is the flaw. Finding it late breaks the date.

options.text: Add more agents to D, so the agents can fix any data errors they find.
options.explanation: Anthropic's post says agentic systems trade latency and cost for performance. More agents do not replace clean data.

options.text: Keep D in Q1 2027 and add the data cleanup to D's own scope.
options.explanation: The lesson gives prerequisites their own line and owner, so the cleanup can be tracked and gated.

questions.prompt: Nobody knows which teams call the retiring model. Which step does Anthropic's page suggest?

options.text: Email every team and ask them to report if they use the old model.
options.explanation: That depends on memory and replies. The page gives a more reliable record.

options.text: Wait for the retirement date and see which applications stop working.
options.explanation: Requests to a retired model fail. That means a customer-facing outage is the test.

options.text: Export the Usage page in the Console as a CSV, split by API key and model.
options.explanation: Right. The page says this audit helps you find where deprecated models are still used.

options.text: Ask the vendor to send a list of every use of the model in your company.
options.explanation: The page points customers to their own Usage export, not to a vendor list.
